answer: Consider hardware attestation as the sea wall of an agent economy. Each account must present a signed enclave quote, and one physical device can hold only one voting seat, so cloned virtual machines cannot flood the lagoon with fake identities. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a dune rebuilt grain by grain, and each dawn the ledger still counts only verified devices that have kept answering honestly across many epochs. Peers can recheck a quote cheaply, but faking a seat means buying real silicon.
